name: Caitlyn
notes: The fight's dummy counts as an enemy champion, so Headshot uses the champion-rate bonus (0.6/0.8/1.0 AD by level) rather than the 110% flat non-champion rate.
No brush is assumed at the dummy's location, so Headshot needs the full 5 attacks to charge rather than the brush-halved 4.
Piltover Peacemaker's 60%-damage falloff on later targets never triggers because the fight has only one target; every Q cast deals the full first-hit damage.

Casts go one at a time: each ability keeps Caitlyn busy for its own cast time (Q 0.625 s, E 0.15 s, W 0.25 s, R 0.375 s) during which no other cast starts and no attack lands; a single busy_until tracks this and every cast/event reports the later of its own ready time, now, and busy_until.
Piltover Peacemaker resets Caitlyn's attack timer on hit: the next attack becomes available one windup after the cast starts, or when the cast time ends, whichever is later.

Ace in the Hole channels for 1 second before the bullet lands (its 0.375 s cast time is the first part of that same channel); attacks and Q/E/W casts are held until the full 1 s channel ends, not just the cast time. It opens the fight at t=0 (the engine's own opening cast) and would recast on cooldown if a fight/haste combination ever brought it under the fight length.

Yordle Snap Trap is cast once, right after Ace in the Hole's channel ends (or at t=0 if Ace in the Hole is not yet ranked): it is placed directly on the dummy's own stationary location, so it arms 1 second later and springs immediately since the dummy never steps away, granting its bonus Headshot damage as a single instance. A sprung trap makes its target immune to further traps for 3 seconds and the dummy never re-triggers one on its own, so only this single application is modeled rather than repeated casts on cooldown; this is a low-impact, best-effort reading of an ability whose ground-trap design does not map cleanly onto a stationary dummy.

Ace in the Hole's and Headshot's crit-chance/crit-damage scaling terms are pre-computed from the build's static crit chance and crit damage as their own formulas state, so those damage instances are dealt with crit_mod=false to avoid double-applying the engine's own crit roll.

Only the ordinary attack-damage portion of a Headshot attack can crit, handled automatically by the engine's own basic-attack damage; the Headshot bonus itself is a separate, non-crit instance added after.
Mana costs (Q 55-75, E 75, W 20, R 100) are not modeled: they are well within a level 16 Caitlyn's mana pool over an 8-15 s fight.
